finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::datasource ssl uses rejectunauthorized:false, so the documented "ssl" toggle gives no mitm protection
evidence: The quoted code is present verbatim in the supplied packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts (`createClient`: `ssl: ds.sslEnabled ? { rejectUnauthorized: false } : false`), so enabling the toggle yields encrypted-but-unauthenticated TLS; since `password: decrypt(ds.password)` is sent in the startup handshake, an active on-path attacker can harvest it and tamper with rows. The new doc page's "**SSL** — toggle on if your database requires it" bullet (datasources.md, Connect a database step 2) does not qualify this, so the documentation-misrepresentation angle also holds. Bounding the severity: the line is pre-existing and untouched by this docs-only diff, the toggle still stops passive sniffing, and exploitation needs a network position between the backend and a user-chosen DB host. I could not confirm the exact line number 204, only that the code sits at the end of `createClient`.
